issue.title: Choose the tech stack and scaffold the app
issue.body:
Pick the stack for the album ranking app and commit a runnable empty scaffold, so every other ticket has something to build on. Follows the stack and shape decisions in the MVP spec (#2).

## Today
The repo has only a README, `.gitignore` and the agent team docs. No code, no test or lint commands (`docs/agents/project.md` § Commands says `none yet`).

## Scope
- Choose the language, framework, package manager and test runner. The shape is fixed by the spec: one web app with a small server and one SQLite file, run on localhost. Write the choice and the reason in a short doc under `docs/`.
- Commit a scaffold that starts locally with one command and shows a blank home page.
- Add one passing smoke test and the commands to run it, a linter and a typecheck if the stack has them.
- Fill the `Test`, `Lint` and `Typecheck` rows in `docs/agents/project.md` § Commands, and the Areas list in § Areas and labels, so later tickets can use them.
- Add a README section for running the app.
- Read config from environment variables, so deploying later needs no rework. No secrets in the repo. Add a `.env.example` if the app reads config.

## Acceptance
- A fresh clone runs the app and the test command with the steps in the README.
- `docs/agents/project.md` § Commands has real values for Test, Lint and Typecheck.
- The stack choice is written down with the reason.

## Out of scope
- Any album, ranking or rating features.
- Database tables (see the data model ticket).
- CI, deployment and a password gate (the deployment ticket).

issue.title: Define the data model and storage for albums, years and rankings
issue.body:
Create the stored shapes and the storage layer the rest of the app reads and writes: albums, artists, per-year placements, matchups and decade lists. Follows the data model outline in the MVP spec (#2) and the scaffold (#3).

## Today
No code or storage exists. The spreadsheet's model, from the MVP spec (#2): one row per album with artist, year, decade, a rank (1 to 10), an honorable mention flag or neither (81 "listed only" rows), and a decade top 25 rank.

## Scope
- Define the entities in the spec's data model outline:
  - **Artist**: name, catalog id (nullable).
  - **Album**: title, artist, catalog id (nullable for manual albums), original release year (nullable), cover art URL (nullable).
  - **Year entry**: album, year, placement (`ranked`, `honorable_mention` or `listed`), rank 1 to 10 when ranked.
  - **Matchup**: album A, album B, result (`a`, `b` or `tie`), created at.
  - **Decade list entry**: decade, album, position 1 to 25, unique per decade. No candidate flag.
  - **Import review item**: the source row's text (title, artist, year, placement), candidate matches, status. Deleted once resolved.
- Store only inputs. Ratings and artist scores are computed from year entries and matchups, never stored.
- Support manual albums (no catalog id) and linking one to a catalog album later, keeping its year entry, matchups and decade list entries.
- Add migrations or an equivalent schema setup on one SQLite file, and a small data access layer with tests.
- Enforce the spec's rules:
  - An album has at most one year entry.
  - Ranks are unique within a year.
  - Honorable mention and listed entries have no order.
  - A decade list entry's album must have a year entry in that decade.
  - Undo deletes the newest matchup row.
  - Deleting an album deletes its matchups.
- The album's year is the year of its year entry, set by the user. The catalog's original release year is stored and is only the default when a row or result has no year. This settles the year question.

## Acceptance
- Tests create, read, update and delete a year entry and reject a second year entry for the same album and a duplicate rank in a year.
- Tests cover the three placements, manual album linking, matchup insert and undo, and the decade list rules.
- Schema setup runs from a clean checkout with the README steps.

## Out of scope
- Catalog search and cover art fetching (separate ticket).
- The Elo math and matchup picking (the Elo engine ticket).
- Importing the spreadsheet.

issue.title: Add album catalog search with cover art
issue.body:
Related: #10

Let the user search a catalog of albums by title and artist and get back results with cover art, so they can add albums to a year without typing them in. Part of the MVP defined in #2.

## Today
No code exists. The spreadsheet holds album and artist names as free text with no catalog id and no cover art.

## Scope
- Choose the catalog and cover art source and write down why. Compare the real options on cost, rate limits, licence and terms for showing covers, cover art coverage for older jazz and 1960s records (about 1960 to 1980 is a large part of the existing list), and whether an API key is needed. These facts were not checked when this ticket was written.
- An album is the catalog's release group, not a pressing or edition (MusicBrainz "release group", Discogs "master", or the nearest equivalent in the chosen source). Reissues, remasters and deluxe editions are the same album and must not appear as separate results.
- Add a search function: input is a free text query, output is a list of albums with title, artist (the catalog's credited artist, so a collaboration is one artist), original release year, a stable catalog id and a cover image URL (or none).
- Call the source from server code only, so an API key is never sent to the browser, and keep keys out of the repo.
- Handle no results, a slow or failing source, and a missing cover (show a placeholder).
- Cache results enough to stay inside the source's rate limits.
- A search box on a page that shows the results with cover, title, artist and original release year.

## Acceptance
- Searching "Getz Gilberto" returns the 1964 album with a cover.
- One album appears once, not once per edition.
- A source error shows a readable message, not a crash.
- Tests cover the search function with the source mocked.

## Out of scope
- Saving an album into a ranking (the ranking screen ticket).
- Bulk matching for the spreadsheet import.

issue.title: Build the per-year ranking screen with drag and drop and covers
issue.body:
A page for one year where the user builds a ranked top 10, honorable mentions and a list of albums they heard but did not place, by dragging album covers, replacing the "Ranked" sheet. Needs catalog search (#5) and the data model (#4). Part of the MVP defined in #2.

## Today
No code exists. In the spreadsheet a year is a row of text: ranks 1 to 10 in order, then an unordered honorable mention list, and in many early years albums with neither (81 rows, mostly 1960 to 1981). Years can have fewer than 10 ranked albums.

## Scope
- A year page (pick any year) with three areas:
  - ten ordered rank slots with cover art,
  - an unordered honorable mention area,
  - an unordered **listed** area for albums heard that year but not placed.
- Add an album from catalog search into any area.
- Reorder by drag and drop, move between a rank slot, honorable mentions and listed, and remove. Changes save to storage.
- Show each album's current rating next to it, from the Elo engine (#7). Listed albums have no rating.
- One album, one year: adding an album that is already on another year page asks to move it.
- Create a manual album (title, artist, year) when the catalog does not have it, shown with the placeholder cover.
- Keyboard-usable reordering and touch drag, so it works without a mouse.
- Empty states for a year with no albums and for a year with fewer than 10 ranked.

## Acceptance
- Dragging an album from rank 4 to rank 1 shifts the others down by one and the order survives a page reload.
- Adding an album already on another year asks to move it, and moving it removes it from the first year.
- A year with 3 ranked albums renders with 7 empty slots and saves.
- Component or end-to-end tests cover add, reorder, move between the three areas and remove.

## Out of scope
- Computing the ratings (the Elo engine ticket).
- Artist and decade views.
- Importing the spreadsheet.

issue.title: Build the Elo rating engine and matchup screen
issue.body:
A rating engine that turns year placements and head-to-head answers into one Elo rating per album, plus the matchup screen where the user answers "which of these two do you like more?". One algorithm, no settings. Needs the data model (#4). Part of the MVP defined in #2; the scoring rules are in the spec's § Scoring.

## Today
No code exists. The spreadsheet's points table, honorable mention value and year weight are not carried over: the spec replaces them with Elo.

## Scope
- **Rating engine.** Pure functions, no UI. Ratings are computed by replay, never stored:
  - Standard Elo: every album starts at 1500, `expected_A = 1 / (1 + 10 ^ ((rating_B - rating_A) / 400))`, `rating_A += K × (score_A - expected_A)` with score 1, 0.5 or 0, and B moves by the same amount the other way. `K = 32`. The constants are fixed in code.
  - Only albums with a ranked or honorable mention placement are rated. Listed albums have no rating.
  - Seeding from year placements: within a year each ranked album beats every album ranked below it and every honorable mention. Honorable mentions do not play each other. Implied results are derived on every replay, not stored.
  - Replay order: implied results first, year by year ascending, higher ranks first; then explicit matchup answers, oldest first.
- **Artist score** as a function: `(sum of ratings + 1500) / (album count + 1)` over the artist's rated albums. The per-decade version uses only albums placed in that decade.
- **Matchup picking:** only albums from different years, never a listed album. Pick the rated album with the fewest explicit matchups (random among ties), then the opponent from another year with the closest rating, skipping a pair already played.
- **Matchup screen:** two album covers side by side. The user picks one, calls a tie, or skips. A skip records nothing and serves the next pair. Undo deletes the last answer. Each answer updates the ratings straight away. A counter shows matchups played.

## Acceptance
- Two new albums at 1500, A wins: A is 1516, B is 1484. A tie between 1500 and 1500 changes nothing. Replaying the same inputs twice gives the same ratings.
- On a fixture year with no explicit matchups, the replay plays exactly the implied results: ranked over lower ranked, ranked over honorable mention, nothing else.
- Answering a matchup changes both ratings. Undo restores the previous ratings exactly.
- The screen never serves two albums from the same year, a listed album, or a pair already played while an unplayed pair exists.
- An artist with albums rated 1600 and 1700 has a score of (1600 + 1700 + 1500) / 3 = 1600.
- Unit tests cover each function with fixed inputs; the screen is covered by a component or end-to-end test.

## Out of scope
- Other scoring algorithms, a settings screen, points tables or year weights.
- Artist and decade pages that show the results (#8, #9).
- Importing the spreadsheet.

issue.title: Add artist views by decade and overall
issue.body:
Related: #9

Pages that rank artists by their score from the Elo ratings, overall and per decade, replacing the Artist Stats and Artist Summary sheets. Needs the Elo rating engine (#7). Part of the MVP defined in #2.

## Today
No code exists. In the spreadsheet, artist rankings are grouped as 60s and 70s, 80s, 90s and 2000s, and 2010s and 2020s, plus an overall rollup. The app ranks one decade at a time instead of the paired groups.

## Scope
- An overall artist ranking list: rank, artist, score, number of rated albums.
- A per-decade artist ranking, one decade at a time with a decade picker (1950s through 2020s). Decades with few albums still render.
- The score is the engine's artist score (#7): `(sum of ratings + 1500) / (album count + 1)` over the artist's rated albums. The per-decade list uses the albums placed in that decade. Listed albums are left out.
- Open an artist to see their albums with cover, year, placement and rating.
- Scores update when a matchup is answered or a year's ranking changes.

## Acceptance
- For an artist with albums rated 1600 and 1700 the list shows a score of 1600.
- An artist with albums in several decades shows the right albums in each decade's list and all of them in the overall list.
- Answering a matchup changes the order where the two albums' artists are listed.
- Tests cover the list building for an artist with albums in several decades.

## Out of scope
- The decade top 25 album lists (separate ticket).
- Changing how artists are scored.
- Matching the spreadsheet's artist summary. The scoring differs on purpose.

issue.title: Add decade top 25 album lists
issue.body:
Per-decade lists of the 25 best albums, hand-ranked as in the spreadsheet, with covers and a rating-based suggestion for decades that have no list yet. Replaces the "Decade Top 25" columns and the By Decade sheet. Related: #8. Needs the Elo rating engine (#7). Part of the MVP defined in #2.

## Today
No code exists. In the spreadsheet 75 albums carry a decade rank, typed by hand: 25 each for the 1960s, 2000s and 2010s. The candidate flag is not used consistently, so it is not carried over.

## Scope
- A decade page listing the top 25 albums with cover, position, artist, year and rating.
- The list is hand-ranked. Any album with a ranked or honorable mention placement in that decade can go on it; the decade is the album's year page decade, not its catalog release year. There is no candidate flag.
- Add albums to the list and reorder by drag and drop, up to 25 per decade. Store each entry in the data model's decade list entry (#4).
- A decade with no list shows a suggestion: its top 25 albums by rating. The user can accept it and then reorder. A suggestion is not saved until accepted.
- Decade picker for every decade that has albums.

## Acceptance
- A decade with fewer than 25 eligible albums renders what it has.
- Reordering persists across reload, and a 26th album is refused.
- An empty decade shows the rating-based suggestion, and nothing is saved until the user accepts it.
- Tests cover list building and the suggestion for a decade.

## Out of scope
- Artist views (#8).
- Importing existing decade ranks (the import ticket).

issue.title: Import the existing spreadsheet
issue.body:
Load the user's `Best Albums.xlsx` into the app, so years of rankings are not retyped. Related: #5. Needs the data model (#4) and catalog search (#5). Part of the MVP defined in #2.

## Today
No code exists. The file is the user's and is not in the repo. Its Albums sheet has 752 album rows, years 1955 to 2024, with columns for rank, album, artist, year, honorable mention flag, decade top 25 candidate flag, decade top 25 rank and the derived scores. The rows are:

- 292 ranked (rank 1 to 10),
- 378 honorable mention,
- 1 ranked and flagged honorable mention (a 2014 row, rank 5),
- 81 listed only (no rank, no honorable mention), mostly 1960 to 1981.

One pair (a 1960 album) is an exact duplicate row. 75 rows carry a decade rank.

## Scope
- A command-line script, run once with the file path. It reads the Albums sheet's input columns (album, artist, year, rank, honorable mention, decade top 25 rank) and creates year entries and decade list entries. It ignores the derived columns, `New`, the candidate flag and the pivot sheets.
- Row mapping: rank becomes ranked; the honorable mention flag becomes honorable mention; neither becomes listed. The flag wins over a rank, as in the sheet, and that row goes to the review page.
- Match each row to a catalog album using catalog search (#5). Auto-accept clear matches. Send ambiguous or missing ones to a review page in the app, which the import fills. There the user picks a match or keeps the row as a manual album.
- Merge exact duplicate rows (same album, same year) into one entry and list them in the summary.
- Safe to re-run: an entry already imported is not added again.
- A summary at the end: rows read, matched, sent to review, merged, skipped.
- Do not commit the spreadsheet, rows from it or any personal data. Test fixtures use made-up rows.

## Acceptance
- After importing the user's file and resolving the review page, every year page shows the sheet's ranks, honorable mentions and listed albums for that year, and the 1960s, 2000s and 2010s decade lists match the sheet's decade ranks. The only differences are the merged duplicate and the rank-plus-honorable-mention row, both named in the summary.
- A second import changes nothing.
- A row with a typo in the title lands in the review page, not the data.
- Tests use a small fixture file of made-up rows covering each row kind, a duplicate and a rank-plus-honorable-mention row.

## Out of scope
- Importing the artist rollup sheets (recomputed by the app).
- Importing the spreadsheet's weighted scores. The app does not use them.
- Exporting back to a spreadsheet.

issue.title: Deploy the app to AWS with staging and production behind a password gate
issue.body:
Put the app on AWS, in a staging and a production environment, so a phone and a laptop see the same rankings behind a password. The MVP runs on localhost only; this is the follow-up named in the MVP spec (#2).

## Today
No code or deployment exists. The app is one Next.js process holding one SQLite file open through `node:sqlite` (`lib/db/server.ts`). The path comes from `DATABASE_PATH` in `lib/config.ts`, defaulting to `./data/album-ranker.db`, and the database migrates itself on first open. Config is read from environment variables. There is no Dockerfile, no hosting config and no password gate. `docs/agents/project.md` § Environments and deploy says "none yet".

## Scope
- The user creates the new AWS account. Creating it, billing, and any credentials or access keys are the user's job and are never committed to the repo. The README says what the user has to set up in the account first, and the deploy steps take credentials from the user's own machine or environment.
- Staging and production both live in that one account. Each has its own running app, its own SQLite file on durable storage, and its own password, so staging never reads or writes production data.
- Choose which AWS service runs the app and write down why. The app must run as exactly one copy with one writer to its SQLite file, and the file must survive restarts and redeploys, so a host with no persistent disk is ruled out unless the spec settles the cost tradeoff below. Say how the SQLite file is kept on durable storage and how it is backed up (backup is copying the file, which includes what is still in the WAL file). Include the rough monthly cost.
- Cost constraint: as much of the AWS deployment as possible is pay-for-what-you-use (billed by requests, compute time or storage used), not long-running services billed while idle. One person uses this occasionally and does not want to pay constantly. This is a constraint on the design, not a choice of service; the spec decides the services. The spec lists each AWS component with how it is billed and an estimated monthly cost at idle for staging and production, and justifies any always-on, idle-billed component.
- The one-copy, one-writer, durable-disk SQLite requirement above may conflict with compute that scales to zero. The spec settles that tradeoff and says what it costs (money, cold starts or anything else). This ticket does not resolve it.
- Deploy the app and its SQLite file to both environments, with config from environment variables or AWS secret storage and no secrets in the repo.
- Add a single shared password gate in front of the whole app: one user, no accounts. The password comes from config, and the app is not reachable without it. Production refuses to start without a password. The password gate is required in staging too, since both are reachable from the internet.
- Serve both environments over HTTPS.
- Write the deploy, promote-to-production and backup and restore steps in the README.
- This exposes personal listening data beyond localhost, so the password gate is required before either environment is reachable from the internet.

## Acceptance
- Staging and production each ask for their own password and show nothing without it.
- Both are served over HTTPS.
- A change made on one device shows on another after reload, in each environment.
- A change made in staging does not show in production.
- The README steps deploy a fresh copy of each environment into an AWS account and restore from a copied database file.
- The spec lists each AWS component with how it is billed and an estimated monthly cost at idle for staging and production, and justifies every always-on, idle-billed component.
- The spec says how the one-copy, durable SQLite requirement is met alongside the cost constraint, and what that costs.
- No AWS credential, secret, `.env` file or database file is committed.

## Out of scope
- Creating the AWS account or handling its credentials. The user does both.
- Accounts, multiple users and sharing.
- Any album, ranking or rating features.
- Local preview environments (see #20) and browser test runs (see #19).
- A custom domain and automatic deploys on merge, unless the user asks for them.

issue.title: feat: ALBUM-5 album catalog search with cover art
issue.body:
Closes #5

ALBUM-5: [Add album catalog search with cover art](https://github.com/dbeallor/album-ranker/issues/5). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-album-5-catalog-search.md`. Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-21-album-5-catalog-search.md`.

## What it does

- `/search` page: a GET search box and server-rendered results with cover, title, credited artist and original year.
- `lib/catalog/`: server-only `searchAlbums(query)` over MusicBrainz release groups (one result per album), covers from Cover Art Archive, a 1.1 s request spacer, 8 s timeout, and a 24 h in-memory cache.
- Readable messages for a busy or failing catalog; a placeholder when a cover fails to load.
- New optional `MUSICBRAINZ_USER_AGENT` setting. No key, no contact details by default.
- Adds the `server-only` package, with a stub alias for Vitest.

## Release note

You can now search albums by title and artist at `/search` and see their covers. Saving an album into a year comes in a later ticket.

## Proof

- **"Getz Gilberto" returns the 1964 album with a cover**: fixture test, catalog mocked (`npx vitest run lib/catalog`):

  ```
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  28 passed (28)
  ```

  Live check against MusicBrainz (`next start`, `/search?q=getz+gilberto`): the page returned the card "Getz / Gilberto", "Stan Getz / João Gilberto featuring Antônio Carlos Jobim", 1964, with cover `https://coverartarchive.org/release-group/b248d212-aace-3c3e-a23d-e13aaac1f87a/front-250`.
- **One album appears once, not once per edition**: results are release groups, deduplicated by id (table test "a release group listed twice appears once").
- **A source error shows a readable message, not a crash**: tests for 503, timeout, 500, network error and malformed JSON; page test renders the message. The first live request hit a real MusicBrainz 503 and the page showed "The album catalog is busy. Try again in a moment."
- **Tests cover the search function with the source mocked**: `lib/catalog/search.test.ts`; full run `npm test` 41 passed, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` clean.

Not proven:
- Cover display in a browser: the cover URL is in the page but no screenshot is attached; missing-cover placeholder is not covered by a test (styling).
